requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data on node1.
requirements.summary: Direct observation showed vg_data/lv_data formatted as XFS and mounted read-write at /srv/data. The final task-state check before the required restart again showed the active 2 GiB LV at that mountpoint.

requirements.requirement: Grow the logical volume to at least 2 GB while it remains mounted and preserve its contents.
requirements.summary: The LV grew online from 1,073,741,824 to 2,147,483,648 bytes. The mount record was identical before and after growth, XFS reported successful online expansion, and both protected-file SHA-256 hashes remained unchanged.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The initial and pre-restart observations both show RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0. The implementation used the platform-installed RHEL lvm2 and XFS tooling, with no package or kernel replacement recorded.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes were directly demonstrated before the provider-mandated restart: the mounted XFS logical volume was grown online to exactly 2 GiB without changing its mount or file contents, and the OS and kernel were retained. Restart persistence was not part of the public contract, so the incomplete restart transition does not reduce those functionality assessments. The separate restart protocol was incomplete because only the healthy pre-restart state and restart acknowledgement were captured; no changed boot identity or recovered service/data state was obtained.
limitations: The node-restart protocol lacks a different post-restart boot identity and recovered service, data, and overall system state. Managed execution and all fixed after-executor observations continued returning connection resets.

Because no post-restart commands succeeded, the final mounted state, checksum persistence, failed-unit state, listening sockets, package health, and temporary-file inventory could not be independently re-observed.
The after-prepare snapshot is an alias of the before-prepare snapshot because preparation was disabled; it establishes the baseline but adds no separate transition observation.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Creating the backing file and loop attachment, LVM objects, filesystem, mount configuration, persistence service, and bounded integrity-test files all had clear roles in implementing or verifying the requested storage outcome; the reboot was required by the provider-wide protocol. However, node1 did not regain managed command availability during more than six minutes of polling, and the fixed after-executor probes also received connection resets. Consequently, final service, package, socket, and residue hygiene could not be checked, and an unresolved post-restart operational problem remains possible.
